finding.claim: D4 conditions replay refill on resident displacement, leaving incoming excess bodies discarded without displacement without a specified recovery transition after capacity is released.
finding.location: D4, paragraph 2: "discard excess bodies without settlement" and "if displacement occurred, replace the watch once"; D4, first and second paragraphs: "a better item displaces a worse unsubmitted item", "discard excess bodies", and "if displacement occurred, replace the watch once"
finding.evidence:
[D4, paragraph 2: "discard excess bodies without settlement" and "if displacement occurred, replace the watch once"] The revised D4 distinguishes replacing a worse resident with a better incoming item from discarding excess bodies. If a full buffer receives worse-ranked items, those incoming bodies are discarded and no resident is displaced. After the retained pages are admitted and acknowledged, the only specified replay/refill trigger is "if displacement occurred", which is false in that case. D3 makes watch the sole mail path, and D4 forbids reconnecting merely because the buffer is full. The design therefore specifies recovery for one form of local body loss while leaving the other without the transition required by its stated "eventual replay after space is released" requirement. This is a defect in the newly added recovery condition, not a request for another capacity bound or a repetition of the earlier missing-capacity finding.
---
[D4, first and second paragraphs: "a better item displaces a worse unsubmitted item", "discard excess bodies", and "if displacement occurred, replace the watch once"] The new capacity fix distinguishes replacing a worse cached item from discarding excess incoming bodies, but conditions its only explicit refill transition on displacement. Consider a full cache followed by items worse than every retained item: the retention rule discards those arrivals and displaces no cached record. Successful page admission and acknowledgements then free space, but the stated replacement condition remains false. The design therefore specifies no refill for this ordinary saturation case, despite requiring "eventual replay after space is released" in the same paragraph. This is a defect in the newly added overflow/replay transition, rather than a demand for autonomous recovery from channel failure: track any discarded pending body as replay debt, not only replacement of a cached body. The pressure-test requirement will expose the contradiction but does not resolve which implementation transition should run.

votes.evidence: D4 in docs/superpowers/runs/2026-11-14-pi-harness/design.md explicitly distinguishes better-item displacement from discarding excess bodies, but gates the post-ACK replacement on displacement. Concrete failure: passive pending frames fill the 2 MiB body/frame budget (near-8-KiB bodies plus framing can exhaust it before the daemon's 256-offer count). Later, worse-ranked frames cannot fit and are discarded, with no resident displaced. D5 permits this cache to remain full indefinitely while settled idle without admitted wake intent. Existing daemon reoffers do not guarantee recovery: src/delivery/ledger.rs:21-24 bounds offers to three per generation at 60-second spacing, and Offer::is_due stops after that count. All those reoffers can occur while the cache is still full. A subsequent ordinary user turn admits and ACKs retained pages under D4/D5, freeing capacity, but displacement is false, so D4 does not replace the watch. ACKing retained IDs does not reset exhausted offers for discarded IDs (ledger remove operates per ID). The existing owner replay is not an ongoing refill safety net: src/service/mod_channels.rs:772-790 captures it once per lease, explicitly making even an empty successful capture terminal; apply_presentation_replay does not recapture it. Thus discarded pending bodies can remain canonical but unavailable to this owner after space is released, contrary to D4's required pressure case of eventual replay after space is released. D1's explicit-inbox fallback and D5's accepted failure-to-start degradation do not define recovery for normal healthy-channel saturation. The first-review disposition at docs/superpowers/runs/2026-11-14-pi-harness/roast-design-1-dispositions.md likewise specifically says replay after displacement; this is an incomplete transition in that capacity fix. Track discarded incoming bodies as replay debt too; this needs no larger cache or stronger runtime-failure guarantee.

(a) Read the entire revised docs/superpowers/runs/2026-11-14-pi-harness/design.md and roast-design-1-dispositions.md. D4 explicitly distinguishes resident displacement from discarding excess incoming bodies, but attaches post-progress watch replacement only to displacement. D3 reload reconciliation and D1 unavailable-channel retry do not cover a healthy saturated channel. Existing replay does not eliminate the case: src/delivery/ledger.rs caps ordinary reoffers at three per generation with 60-second spacing (Offer::is_due), while src/service/mod_channels.rs::presentation_replay_snapshot/apply_presentation_replay captures one finite replay pass per lease, including a terminal empty capture, and does not recapture it when ACKs free space. Thus automatic reoffers can be exhausted while passive idle content legitimately occupies capacity; later ACKs of retained content do not themselves promise another replay of discarded bodies. (b) D4 expressly requires eventual replay after space is released. Its degraded outcome is for failed replay, and D5 accepts bounded recovery from runtime wake failure; neither accepts omission of replay after ordinary overflow. (c) This concerns the stated finite buffer and normal supported passive-idle behavior, not larger capacity or unconditional runtime recovery. (d) On saturation, worse incoming bodies can be discarded with zero resident replacements. After retained pages succeed, the named replacement predicate remains false and discarded canonical mail can stay unavailable to boundary delivery even with freed space. Durable retention prevents data loss, so Should-fix rather than Blocking. The pressure-test requirement states the desired outcome but does not repair this narrower recovery condition. Track any discarded unacknowledged body as replay debt, or explicitly supply an equivalent refill transition. This is internal evidence only; no external API premise is required.

The internal premises hold. design.md D4 (docs/superpowers/runs/2026-11-14-pi-harness/design.md:43-45) distinguishes displacement of a worse resident from discarding excess incoming bodies, but predicates its explicit post-progress watch replacement on displacement. A cache containing the first 256 equal-priority items can discard later, worse-by-creation arrivals without replacing any resident. After those retained pages are admitted and acknowledged, that predicate remains false. Searching the complete design for replay, refill, reconnect, discard, displacement and pending found lifecycle/reload recovery (D1/D3), failed-channel recovery, and qualification requirements, but no ordinary post-capacity-release trigger for this case. The earlier disposition repeats the same limited condition (docs/superpowers/runs/2026-11-14-pi-harness/roast-design-1-dispositions.md:9). Existing machinery does not supply an unconditional guarantee: legacy watch assembly suppresses previously emitted IDs (src/delivery/assemble.rs:302,357); V2 owner replay captures a lease-scoped pass once and removes completed stamps, with even an empty capture terminal for that lease (src/service/mod_channels.rs:743-838). Ordinary timed reoffers are bounded (src/delivery/ledger.rs), not guaranteed recovery after arbitrarily delayed space release. D4 explicitly requires eventual replay after space is released, so its pressure-test requirement exposes rather than resolves the missing transition. This is an incomplete recovery condition, not permanent data loss: canonical pending state remains intact. Track any discarded pending body as replay debt, including incoming excess, and consume that debt through the existing progress-triggered replacement.
